extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys/agents), USPTO OED staff, and respondents in disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and standards for imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including service requirements, respondent's opportunity to contest (40‑day response), determination standard, and publication/notice obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline authority (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline (e.g., public reprimand) based on disciplinary action taken by a State disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order applies reciprocal discipline pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59. In practice, a state disciplinary action (e.g., public reprimand) can be the basis for imposing the same discipline at the USPTO unless a respondent establishes grounds under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) that make identical discipline unwarranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's obligation to contest: 40‑day response (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent seeks to contest imposition of identical discipline, they must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information the respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response must specifically present facts or legal arguments showing a genuine issue of material fact that would make imposing discipline identical to the state discipline unwarranted under the limited grounds in § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to file such a response permits a finding that no genuine issue exists and that reciprocal discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements and service by publication (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.11, 11.24(b), 11.35(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order must be mailed to the most recent address provided by the respondent to OED under 37 C.F.R. § 11.11; if mailing is returned unclaimed, service by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24(b) and 11.35(b) is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example on this page: Notice mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the street address in respondent's record; mailing was returned as 'unclaimed,' and a service by publication notice was published in the Official Gazette (dates provided). The service method used affects when and how the respondent may obtain copies and be considered notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground constituting violation for USPTO discipline: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) by having been publicly reprimanded on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This regulation provides a basis for USPTO disciplinary action where a state disciplinary authority has publicly reprimanded a practitioner on ethical grounds. The USPTO's notice here states the respondent violated § 10.23(b)(6) because of the Oregon State Bar's public reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: State disciplinary grounds as basis for federal action (example: Oregon DR 1-102(A)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary rules (here Oregon Disciplinary Rule DR 1-102(A)(2)) may identify conduct (e.g., conviction for unlawful possession of marijuana) that results in state discipline and thereby trigger reciprocal discipline at the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites the Oregon State Bar Disciplinary Board's reprimand for violating DR 1-102(A)(2) by being convicted of unlawful possession of marijuana as the factual/legal basis for the state reprimand that led to USPTO action. State rule violations and underlying facts will typically be summarized in the Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations following discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: After imposing discipline, the OED Director must publish the Final Order, publish a notice in the Official Gazette, post disciplinary decisions in the OED Reading Room, and give notice of the discipline and reasons to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where the practitioner is admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific actions ordered here: (a) public reprimand; (b) OED Director shall publish the Final Order; (c) publish the Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette (example notice text is provided); (d) give notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts per § 11.59. The Reading Room URL is cited as a location where such decisions are posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to respond to Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a timely response contesting the imposition of identical discipline, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and that reciprocal discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On these facts, respondent did not file a response; consequently, under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) the Director determined (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact and (2) a public reprimand is appropriate. This illustrates that silence or non-response can lead to automatic imposition of the requested reciprocal discipline.
